name: Class III All-Terrain Vehicle
description: A motorcycle that travels on two tires while it's being ridden off the highway, which is how Oregon classes an electric dirt bike on trails and riding areas. Defined by Oregon Revised Statutes §801.194 and regulated by ORS chapter 821.
restrictions: A two-wheeled motorcycle being ridden off the highway; no limit on motor power or speed
Needs an ATV operating permit and decal from Oregon Parks and Recreation, valid for two years, to ride where the land manager requires one
Riders 16 or older need an ATV safety education card on public lands
Riders under 16 need the card and a hands-on course, and must be accompanied by someone 18 or older who holds an ATV card
Riders under 7 may not ride on public lands
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet with the chin strap fastened
Kept off highways, their shoulders and medians, except to cross, load or unload, or where posted open to all-terrain vehicles
No insurance needed off the highway
